module_title: Properties of Matter and Fluids (Basic / Foundational)
introduction: This foundational level covers the elastic behavior of solids and the core principles governing fluids at rest (hydrostatics), such as Pascal's law and Archimedes' principle. Mastering these basics is essential for scoring in direct, formula-based questions in NEET and JEE Main.

core_concepts.title: Stress and Strain
core_concepts.description: Stress is the internal restoring force acting per unit area of a deformed body ($\text{Stress} = F/A$). Strain is the fractional change in the dimensions of the body ($\text{Strain} = \Delta L / L$). Strain is completely dimensionless.

core_concepts.title: Hooke's Law
core_concepts.description: Within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain ($\text{Stress} \propto \text{Strain}$). The constant of proportionality is called the Modulus of Elasticity ($E$).

core_concepts.title: Pascal's Law
core_concepts.description: If the effect of gravity is neglected, the pressure applied to any point of an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished to every other portion of the fluid. This forms the basis of hydraulic lifts.

core_concepts.title: Archimedes' Principle
core_concepts.description: When a body is partially or wholly immersed in a fluid, it experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the body.

important_entities.name: Young's Modulus ($Y$)
important_entities.significance: Strictly defined only for solids (like wires). A higher Young's Modulus means a material is more elastic because it resists deformation strongly. For example, steel is physically more elastic than rubber.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In everyday speech, 'elastic' means easily stretchable (like rubber). In physics, elasticity is the ability to recover the original shape. Since steel requires vastly more force to deform than rubber for the same strain, steel has a higher modulus and is more elastic.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always remember that the density used must belong to the fluid ($\rho_{\text{fluid}}$), NOT the solid object. Similarly, the volume is only the portion of the object currently resting below the surface.

exam_strategy_tips: Pressure is a scalar quantity, even though the force producing it has a specific direction perpendicular to the surface.
In graphical questions, the slope of the linear region in a Stress-Strain curve directly yields the Modulus of Elasticity.
